title: Upstream branch opportunities for the cephalopod-ai Trilium fork
limitations: Static source and Git graph assessment; no runtime, build, test or performance validation performed.
All branch heads inventoried and triaged; selected candidates received deeper source review. This is not a complete security audit of all heads.
Unmerged means unique commits versus upstream main; it does not prove missing functionality or an active pull request.
Net patches use each head's merge base with upstream main. Apply checks use the frozen fork bare index; failure in both directions is not a semantic conflict test.
Stable patch equivalence was restricted to same-subject non-merge candidates; absence of a match is not proof of novelty.
PR change counts are GitHub API base/head snapshots; branch merge-base net diffs can include different totals.
Git clean merge/apply results are structural only, never a release-readiness or security guarantee.
Live branches/PRs can change after the pinned snapshot.

data_sources: Live paginated GitHub branches and open-pulls REST APIs through authenticated gh (read only)
Fetched all 96 upstream branch heads and 13 supplemental external PR heads into an external bare repository
Git ancestry, merge-base net diffs, stable patch IDs, current-fork source comparison
Non-mutating cached-index apply checks for all85 unmerged heads plus13 supplemental PR heads
git merge-tree structural checks for11 selected refs including upstream main
methodology.catalog: Private catalog searched with repo_path. Optimization workflow inspected but not admitted: feature/branch adoption triage is outside its runtime-efficiency audit scope.
methodology.writing: Local Markdown/JSON follows existing repository audit destinations; write-page writing guidance applied without remote Page edits.

open_pull_requests.title: feat(client): template badge and template properties dialog
open_pull_requests.body:
Builds a UI on top of `#template:titleTemplate` (948a913514, already on `main`, closes #5080): a badge that marks template notes and a properties dialog for what a template sets on the notes created from it.

## Template badge

A note with `#template` or `#workspaceTemplate` shows a badge in the title row, next to the snippet badge. Attributes on a template reach every note created from it through `~template`, so an edit made to a template has effects outside the note being edited. The badge and its tooltip make that visible where the edit happens.

- It reads _Template_ for a global template and _Workspace template_ for a note with only `#workspaceTemplate`. A note with both labels counts as global.
- It uses the `bx-copy-alt` icon of the Note menu's _Template_ toggle and a new cream color: `--badge-template-background-color` (`#ece0c0` light, `#7d6f52` dark), plus a `--badge-template-text-color` token. Badges draw white text, which cream cannot carry in the light theme.

## Global or workspace scope

The badge opens a dropdown with two checkable rows, _Available everywhere_ (`#template`) and _Only inside its workspace_ (`#workspaceTemplate`).

- The workspace row is disabled, with the reason in its tooltip, unless an ancestor owns `#workspace`. The ancestry walk follows `getParentNotes()` rather than `getAllNotePaths()`, which yields nothing for a note whose path to root is not loaded.
- A workspace template outside any workspace can still be switched back to global.
- The new label is set before the old one is removed, so the note never stops being a template in between. Both writes go through `attributes.setBooleanWithInheritance`, as the Note menu's toggle does, so an inherited label is overridden with `=false`.

## Template properties dialog

The dropdown's _Template properties..._ opens a dialog laid out like a collection's properties (`CollectionPropertiesDialog`, a column of cards). Its _New notes_ card has two settings:

- **Default title of created notes:** the template's own `#template:titleTemplate`. The field is the bulk rename's `TemplateField`, set up with the variables `getNewNoteTitle()` passes on the server (`now`, `parentNote`), so expressions are colored, completed and checked by the rules the server applies. Below it, a preview fills the template in with the current time, with the template's own parent standing in for `parentNote` (a template has no fixed parent for its notes). `TemplateField` gains a `preview` prop for that, and an `onBlur` prop.
- **Default location of created notes:** a `NoteAutocomplete` editing the template's own `~template:newNoteDefaultParent`. Picking a note saves it through the `set-attribute` route; clearing the field removes it. Where the relation is set several times, the picker shows and replaces the first one.

As in the collection dialogs there is no Save button. The title is written when the field loses focus and again when the dialog closes, and an unchanged value writes nothing; the location is written as it is picked. Both fields start from the template's **owned** attribute only, so a value inherited from a Templates folder is never copied onto the template by opening and closing the dialog.

## Documentation

- _Note badges_ describes the template badge, its scope switch and the dialog.
- _Templates_ points to the dialog from its default-title and default-parent sections.

## Testing

- `NoteBadges.spec.tsx`: which notes get the badge and its wording, when the workspace row is disabled, the order of the label switch, and the properties row triggering `showTemplateProperties`.
- `template_properties.spec.tsx`: saving the title on blur and on close (and not saving an unchanged one), the variables passed to the field, the preview, the destination picker setting and removing the relation, and an inherited value left out of the field.
- `TemplateField.spec.tsx`: a preview given by the caller wins over the note's.
- Each new assertion was checked against a mutation of the code it covers.
- `pnpm typecheck`.

open_pull_requests.title: feat(share): let guests edit a shared text note with the app's own editor
open_pull_requests.body:
First tier of the collaboration feature, rebuilt as an addition to Sharing after #12022 was closed as too large: a shared **text** note can be opened to editing by the visitors of its page, without accounts. Later tiers add other note types and adding notes, then live updates, presence and cursors — each as its own PR.

> The branch is cut from #12043, so that fix's commit sits beneath this one; merging #12043 first drops it from here.

## For the host

- The Shared badge's menu gains **Guests can edit**. Turning it on opens a dialog that asks how the page is unlocked: **with a password** guests enter on the page, or **anyone with the link**, behind a warning. **Allow attachments** lets guests upload images and files into the notes they edit; **Set/Change the password…** reopens the dialog.
- The settings are three inheritable labels on the note, written by one server route (`PUT /api/notes/:noteId/share-edit`): `#shareEdit`, `#shareEditPassword` (`<salt>$<scrypt>` in base64, the app's own scrypt) and `#shareAttachments`. No migration, no sync-protocol change. The note that owns `#shareEdit` is the *edit root*: its password unlocks the subtree as a whole.
- In the tree, a shared note guests can edit shows the group icon instead of the share icon; the badge does too. Every guest change that is due a revision gets one of the new source `collab`, shown as *Guest edit* in the revisions dialog.
- The options appear only on the server and the desktop (share scopes `public` and `local`); standalone and mobile serve no pages and change nothing.

## For the guest

- A text page asks `GET /share/api/edit/session?noteId=` whether its note is editable and shows an **Edit** button beside the title. `POST /share/api/edit/login` verifies the password, regenerates the session, stores a grant keyed by the edit root, and answers a CSRF token, the note's `blobId` and the payload a hosted view normally finds embedded in its page.
- The page then replaces its rendered content with the app's own `EditableText` widget — classic toolbar above the note — mounted through `ShareAppHost` with a new `readOnly={false}` prop, after `prepareAppHost()` (extracted from `app_view.ts`) has loaded the app's globals and locale. The title is edited in place.
- Saves go through `PUT /share/api/notes/:noteId/data` naming the version the editor loaded; a save over a newer version is refused with `409` and the page shows a banner offering to reload or to keep the visitor's version. Uploads go through `POST /share/api/notes/:noteId/attachments/upload` and come back as the share's own `api/attachments/<id>/image/<title>` (or `…/download`) URL, which the app resolves the same way from its root. **Stop editing** saves what is pending and reloads the rendered page; **Log out** drops the grant.

## What guests cannot do, by design

- Only text notes without `#readOnly`; no type change; no adding, moving or deleting notes.
- Content goes through the sanitizer imported HTML goes through, with inline `data:` images and include-note sections dropped. Internal links are not turned into relations (that happens when the host saves).
- The editor runs without the plugins that reach the host's other notes or services — cut to note, include note, internal links, link embeds, Markdown import, snippets, AI assistant, block references, icon picker, note mentions, slash commands — and without the upload plugins unless attachments are allowed; the matching toolbar items are hidden.
- The guest routes are CSRF-protected under the session the login issued, rate-limited (the login limiter shared with `/login`; 1200 saves/minute; 300 uploads per 15 minutes; 20 MB per upload; 2 MB per save) and never set `session.loggedIn`, so `/api/*` stays closed to guests. `SECURITY.md` says what is in scope.

## Core and client plumbing

- `SNote` treats `#shareEditPassword` as a secret like `#shareCredentials`: `getAttributes()`, `getPojo()` and `buildFrocaRows()` leave both out, and `getSecretLabelValue()` reads one for the server. `isShareNoteReadable()` is exported so the guest routes apply the share's own credential and protected-note checks. `SHARED_OPTIONS`/`getAppAssetPath()` are exported from the renderer for the login payload.
- `services/server.ts` sends the component id and the CSRF token on a shared page that edits, refreshes the token from `glob.csrfRefreshUrl`, and has `putWithSilentConflict()`; `useEditorSpacedUpdate`'s `commit` branches on `isShareEditing()`; `getDisabledPlugins()`/`buildToolbarConfig()` gate the plugins and items; `getTemplates()` offers nothing on a share.
- `saveRevisionIfNeeded(note, source)` takes the revision source; `REVISION_SOURCES` gains `collab`.

## Docs

`Sharing.md` gains a *Letting guests edit* section and the attribute table rows; `SECURITY.md` gains the guest-editing scope. The in-app help HTML of the Sharing page is regenerated.

## Verification

- Specs, written red first against `main`: core `collab/share_edit.spec.ts` and `collab/guest_writes.spec.ts` (run on both the server and the standalone runner), `snote.spec.ts`/`froca_payload.spec.ts` for the secret label, server `collab/routes.spec.ts` (supertest: session, login 401/200, CSRF 403, stale 409, 413, title, upload 403/200, logout 401, read-only, closing), share-theme `page/share_edit.spec.ts`, `content/edit_view.spec.tsx`, `app_host.spec.tsx`, and client specs for `server.ts`, `hooks.tsx`, `config.ts`, `toolbar.ts`, `snippets.ts`, the badge hook and the dialog.
- Coverage gates: `npx vitest run share --coverage` in `apps/server` (182 tests) and `apps/standalone` (161 tests) with their 100% thresholds; `pnpm --filter @triliumnext/share-theme test --coverage` at 100%.
- `pnpm typecheck` clean; format lint on changed lines clean apart from the pre-existing style of the objects touched (`quote-props` in `app_context.ts`/`attr_help.ts`, bracket spacing of `REVISION_SOURCES`).
- A headless-Chromium probe against a throwaway dev server: share a text note, open editing with a password from the host API, unlock on the page, type and see the save, rename the title, provoke a stale save and see the banner, keep the guest's version, allow attachments and see the upload button, stop editing, log out, close editing.

open_pull_requests.title: feat(sort): add #sortArchivedLast to sort archived notes last (closes #10615)
open_pull_requests.body:
Adds a `#sortArchivedLast` label, as asked in the issue. On a parent with `#sorted`, it puts the archived children below all the other ones, whatever the `#sortDirection`.

## Behavior

It follows the precedence rcswift proposed in the issue: archived/non-archived is checked first, and `#top`, `#bottom`, `#sortFoldersFirst` and the `#sorted` levels then only order the notes within each group. So:

- an archived note with `#top` still sorts below a non-archived note with `#bottom`
- with `#sortFoldersFirst`, archived folders sort below the non-archived leaf notes but above the archived leaf notes
- without the label, nothing changes

## Changes

- `tree.ts`: new `archivedLast` parameter on `sortNotes()`, read from the label in `sortNotesIfNeeded()`.
- `handlers.ts`: a parent is re-sorted when `#sortArchivedLast` changes, and when a child's `#archived` label is added or removed under a parent that uses it. The list of sorting label names is now a `SORTING_LABELS` constant shared by the two subscribers.
- `sortArchivedLast` is registered as a built-in boolean label, with attribute help text (en only).
- Documented in the Sorting Notes and Labels pages of the User Guide, help HTML regenerated with `docs.mjs sync`.

## Testing

- `tree.spec.ts`: ordering with `#top`/`#bottom` on both archived and non-archived notes, `#sortDirection=desc` together with `#sortFoldersFirst`, and the default order without the label. The first two fail without the change.
- `handlers.spec.ts`: an `#archived` change re-sorts the parent only when it has `#sortArchivedLast`, and a `#sortArchivedLast` change re-sorts the note itself. Fails without the change.
- The tree and handlers specs pass under both the server and the standalone runners. `pnpm typecheck` is clean.

Closes #10615

open_pull_requests.title: fix(client): keep a tab's scroll position when its width changed while hidden (closes #11630)
open_pull_requests.body:
Closes #11630.

A text note lost its scroll position when you switched to another tab and back, if the width changed in between: a sidebar opened or closed, the window was resized, or (on the old layout) the right pane came back a frame after the tab. Images resized in percent make it worst, since their height follows the width.

## Cause

A tab in the background is `display: none`. When it is shown again, the browser restores the old `scrollTop` in pixels, but the content above has reflowed at the new width, so the same offset shows another part of the note. The browser's own scroll anchoring cannot correct this, since the hidden container has no earlier layout to compare against.

Bisecting between v0.104.0 and v0.105.0 points to cc6e89046c, the merge that stopped loading `ckeditor5-premium-features.css`. That stylesheet gives `.ck.ck-editor__editable::before` a full-size, absolutely positioned overlay, and Chrome picked it as the scroll anchor, which kept the old offset through the reflow. Loading only that stylesheet on the bad commit, or only that one rule, makes the drift go away. Without it, the underlying problem shows up again. Resizing the window while the tab is hidden also drifts on v0.104.0.

## Fix

`ScrollingContainer` (`apps/client/src/widgets/containers/scrolling_container.ts`) records the block at the top of the view and its offset once per frame while scrolling. A `ResizeObserver` notices when the container is shown again after being hidden and scrolls that block back to the same offset before the next paint. The lookup and the restore are in `scroll_anchor.ts`. Nothing is restored when the container was at the top, or when the recorded block is no longer in the note.

## Testing

- New specs: `scroll_anchor.spec.ts` (picking the anchor, skipping inline, positioned and hidden boxes, scrolling only when the block moved) and `scrolling_container.spec.ts` (restoring after a hide and show, keeping the anchor through a scroll event while hidden, leaving a resize while shown and the top of the note alone, cleanup). The restore specs fail without the fix.
- The client suite passes. `pnpm typecheck` is clean.
- Manually in the web client, with a long note scrolled to a paragraph and the window resized while another tab was active: the same paragraph is at the top when switching back, within a pixel, with images resized in percent, images at their original size, and text only. Switching tabs without a resize, resizing while the note is shown, and opening another note in the tab (which scrolls to the top) behave as before. On v0.105.0 with the old layout, the right-pane case from the issue also keeps its position with this change.

open_pull_requests.title: fix(text): keep the selection drawn after pressing an included note (closes #11650)
open_pull_requests.body:
Closes #11650.

After clicking an included note, the text editor stopped drawing its selection. Deleting the include left the caret where it was, and typing over a double-clicked word left the typed characters selected (typing "XYZ" over "charlie" gave "Z delta" with the "Z" still selected). It also happened without deleting anything, and it lasted until a tab switch or a reload.

## Cause

`preventCKEditorHandling()` in `packages/ckeditor5/src/plugins/content_embed/content_embed.ts` sets the private `view._renderer.isFocused` to `false` when the include is pressed, so the browser does not draw a stray caret inside it. CKEditor binds that flag to `view.document.isFocused` and only syncs it again when the editor's focus changes. The editor keeps the focus through the press, so the flag stayed `false` and the renderer stopped writing the model selection to the DOM.

## Fix

`ContentEmbedEditing` now listens to `change:range` on the model selection and, once the selection is no longer on an include, sets `_renderer.isFocused` back to `view.document.isFocused`. A new press on the include still turns it off as before.

## Testing

- New specs in `content_embed.spec.ts`: the flag comes back once the selection leaves the include (and a second press turns it off again), and once the selected include is deleted, with the DOM caret in the new empty paragraph. Both fail without the fix.
- The ckeditor5 browser suite passes, with `content_embed.ts` at 100% coverage. `pnpm typecheck` is clean.
- Manually in the web client: after Backspace deletes an include, the caret sits in the empty paragraph, and typing "XYZ" over "charlie" gives "second paragraph XYZ delta". Clicking an include and then clicking back into the text also works without deleting it.

open_pull_requests.title: fix(render): show script modals above app chrome
open_pull_requests.body:
Fixes #11847

## Problem

A Render Note that opens the public `trilium:preact` Modal shows the dialog behind the note title and its own backdrop. Its content cannot be clicked, although Escape can dismiss it.

## Root cause

The public API exported the internal Modal directly. It therefore rendered inline inside the Render Note's scrolling, contained note detail, while Bootstrap created the backdrop under `document.body`. Those nodes are in different stacking contexts, so the dialog's normal z-index could not lift it over the backdrop or note title. Render Note also cleared its JSX container without unmounting the Preact tree, which could leave a body-level portal behind on refresh or disposal.

Portaling the Modal to `body` fixes that layering but removes its original DOM ancestors. Internal note links use the nearest `data-ntx-id` ancestor to select a pane, and Render Note CSS uses `@scope (.render-note-scope)`. The portal must preserve those two parts of the source context.

## Solution

- Expose a script Modal wrapper that reads its source pane and Render Note scope before portaling the existing Modal beside Bootstrap's body-level backdrop. A boxless wrapper carries `data-ntx-id` and, for Render Notes, `render-note-scope`. Nested script modals inherit both. Ordinary script modals do not acquire Render Note styling. The internal Modal and `openDialog` remain in use.
- Unmount a Render Note's prior Preact root before replacing it and when its view is disposed. Ignore asynchronous bundle results after refresh or unmount so they cannot recreate a stale portal.

This uses the existing Preact portal and Modal mechanisms, without a z-index override or a parallel overlay system.

## Testing

- Reproduced with the reporter's ZIP on `upstream/main` at `d5bbfe74f8a3bc34eefbfb2d07cd2e9a3aa7e095`. Before: the title was clipped and hit testing at the dialog returned the backdrop. After the original portal fix: the dialog was above the backdrop and clickable, including its close button.
- Follow-up targeted Vitest: 5 files, 70 tests passed. Tests cover body-level mounting, Preact context and cleanup, source-pane ancestry, scoped-style ancestry, nested script modals, ordinary Modal behavior, and Render Note cancellation/disposal. The new assertions failed with the old body-only portal and passed after the fix; the unmount test failed when its abort cleanup was temporarily removed.
- Local V8 report for the targeted suite marks all 25 changed executable production lines as covered. The Codecov patch gate will be re-evaluated by CI.
- `pnpm typecheck`: passed. Client production build: passed. `git diff --check`: passed. Targeted CSS stylelint passed on the original change; no CSS files changed in this follow-up.
- Targeted ESLint still reports errors on unchanged baseline lines in `Modal.tsx`; the new Render test lints cleanly. The repository's format-only ESLint config does not select TSX files.
- A real Chromium DOM check confirmed `@scope` reaches content under the boxless wrapper, the source pane remains discoverable, and hit testing reaches the modal above the backdrop. A full Trilium walkthrough of this follow-up hit repeated Chrome renderer timeouts, so it is not claimed as passed.

## Scope

Only the client script API, Modal wrapper, Render Note JSX lifecycle, and related tests changed. No server, database, sync, storage, dependencies, or unrelated UI behavior changed.

open_pull_requests.title: feat(relations): reify one statement as a note
open_pull_requests.body:
## Why

A relation stays an edge until something needs to talk about that one instance. Argument graphs need the statement itself to be a note, so another relation can point at it. This is the relation-reification slice of the spike in #11791: one statement becomes a note, and the maps can fold that fact and point other relations at it.

## What

- Asking for a relation creates one note for that row, titled like `supports(Claim, Evidence)`, and files it under `_reifications`. The attribute stays. A title that was edited by hand is left alone. Renaming an endpoint rewrites a generated title. Deleting the attribute removes the note.
- The relation's name can be its own note, apart from any one instance of it.
- On a relation map, clicking the arrow folds the two notes and the arrow into that note. Right-click puts them back. Relations of the fact are drawn on the folded note. Rename still uses the name popover.
- On a link map, the same fold happens in place. A relation between two facts is drawn between those edges while both stay unfolded. Unfolding puts the two notes back where they were.

## Test plan

- [ ] From the attribute list, turn one relation into a note and open it. Attach another relation to that note.
- [ ] On a relation map, click an arrow to fold it, right-click the circle to expand it, and use Back.
- [ ] On a link map, fold a relation, then a relation of that fact, and unfold in place.

open_pull_requests.title: feat(collections): add a timeline view
open_pull_requests.body:
A first, minimal **Timeline** collection view (`#viewType=timeline`), in the spirit of the timeline AppFlowy shipped in 0.14.4 and Notion's — built on FullCalendar Premium's resource timeline rather than a renderer of our own.

## What it does

- **Rows follow the note tree.** Every note of the collection is a row, nested like the tree and in branch order (`resources.ts`); a clone gets one row, under the first parent reached. Notes outside the subtree (a search collection's results) follow as flat rows.
- **Bars come from the calendar's labels.** `#startDate` / `#endDate` / `#startTime` / `#endTime`, including the `#calendar:startDate` remaps, via the calendar's own `buildEvents()` — so a collection switches between Calendar and Timeline without touching its notes.
- **Editing:** drag or resize a bar to change its dates (the calendar's `changeEvent()`); select a range on a row to date that row's note, which is how an undated note gets onto the timeline. Bars can't be dragged to another row.
- **Clicking** a bar or a row title opens the calendar's `EventPopover`.
- **Adding notes:** a + in the left column's header creates a note in the collection; a + on each row (on hover) creates a child of that row's note. Both open the new note in the popover to name and date it.
- **Scales:** Week / Month / Year (the year in week columns, so every scale snaps to the day), the last one kept in `#timeline:view`.
- New `_template_timeline` built-in template (marked beta), a `Collections/Timeline` User Guide page wired as the view's help page.

Not in this draft: dependencies, progress, group-by, property columns, summary bars for undated parents, printing.

## Licensing

FullCalendar Premium (`fullcalendar-scheduler@7.1.0`) is tri-licensed — commercial, CC BY-NC-ND, AGPLv3. Since v7 the open-source option is **AGPLv3** (it was GPLv3 before), for projects "whose frontend and backend are fully AGPLv3-compliant". Trilium is AGPL and has carried no proprietary component since the CKEditor premium features were dropped, so the condition holds. Unlike the CKEditor case, the source is public (`fullcalendar/fullcalendar-workspace/premium`), the rights pass to forks, and the preset key `AGPL-My-Frontend-And-Backend-Are-Open-Source` is a local string comparison with no network call.

The npm metadata says only `SEE LICENSE IN LICENSE.md` (also for its `@full-ui/headless-grid` dependency), so SBOM tools will show it as unknown; the README license section now names it explicitly.

## Dependencies

- `fullcalendar-scheduler` pins `fullcalendar` to the exact same version, so Renovate's FullCalendar group now includes it.
- The lockfile also drops the stale `@parcel/watcher` entries — already under `ignoredOptionalDependencies`, pruned by pnpm on any lockfile write.

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter client test timeline/resources NoteList CollectionProperties in_app_help services/i18n collection-properties` — green.
- `pnpm --filter server test hidden_subtree_templates` and `pnpm --filter standalone test hidden_subtree_templates` — green.
- `pnpm typecheck` — no errors in the touched files.
- `docs.mjs check` — 0 errors.

open_pull_requests.title: feat(server): let an operator allowlist a Tailscale tailnet node for API calls (closes #11422)
open_pull_requests.body:
## Why

Closes #11422. An AI/LLM custom provider pointed at a Tailscale node fails: its `100.64.0.0/10` address is carrier-grade NAT, which `safe_fetch` refuses. The error message shown is `URLs pointing to link-local or carrier-grade NAT addresses are not allowed`. There was no override path.

## What

Adds `TRILIUM_SAFE_FETCH_ALLOWLIST`: a comma-separated list of exact addresses or CIDRs read in `apps/server/src/services/request.ts` and threaded to `safeFetch` as `SafeFetchPolicy.allowedAddresses`.

The list opens only carrier-grade-NAT addresses, only on the relaxed `fetchApi` path (the operator-chosen-destination call), and never on the strict `fetchResource` path that loads a note's linked resource. Anti-rebinding DNS pinning is unchanged.

`parseAllowlist` returns the dropped tokens alongside the entries it accepted, so `request.ts` parses the env once at module load and logs one info-level line naming every unparseable token. The rest of the list stays in force. Tokens are read once.

## Testing and Validation

I've manually tested this in a flatpak build.

Also, `safe_fetch.spec.ts` is 44 tests passing — 9 added in two groups:

- 5 for the operator-policy allowlist behaviour (single-address match, scope to listed addresses, CIDR membership, strict-path non-application, end-to-end through `safeFetch`).
- 4 for the `parseAllowlist`: empty input, all-valid, mixed valid-and-invalid (whitespace-only tokens stay silent), and the realistic operator-typo set (hostname, too many octets, malformed CIDR network part, mask out of range).

Run:

```
pnpm --filter server test safe_fetch.spec.ts
```

`pnpm typecheck` reports no errors. The strict-path test (`validateHostResolution("100.83.121.222", false, ["100.83.121.222"])`) still rejects — note content cannot steer the server to a tailnet node, even one on the operator's list.

## Scope

- `safe_fetch.ts` is unchanged in default behaviour: when the env var is unset, the allowlist is empty and reachable ranges are exactly as before.
- `SafeFetchPolicy.allowedAddresses` is the new optional policy field. `safe_fetch` re-parses each call; the warning happens once at module load.
- A typo'd entry no longer fails silently — operators see the dropped tokens at process start.
- The strict `fetchResource` path does not consult the allowlist at all.

open_pull_requests.title: feat(text): double-click expands inline diagrams, formulas and code blocks
open_pull_requests.body:
Double-clicking an inline diagram, formula or code block inside a text note now expands it. Requested for Mermaid code blocks, which rendered at note width with no way to read a large graph; the same gesture covers the other inline things that have the same problem.

## Behaviour

Follows the existing image convention: where a note exists, double-click opens it; otherwise the content opens in a lightbox.

- **Included Mermaid note** (Include Note of a `mermaid` note): double-click navigates to that note in the current tab, Ctrl+click or middle-click opens it in a new tab, exactly like an image in a text note.
- **Mermaid code block** (`language-mermaid`), in both the editor preview and the read-only view: opens a lightbox with the diagram in a zoom/pan viewer.
- **Math formula** (KaTeX, inline or display), both modes: opens the same lightbox, scaled up to fit.
- **Code block**, read-only view only: opens the lightbox with the code in the shared `CodeBlock` component (copy button, word-wrap follows the `codeBlockWordWrap` option). Not bound in the editor, where double-click is the word-selection gesture.
- Double-click only; the only added chrome is `cursor: zoom-in` on the expandable elements (`pointer` on an included diagram, since that one navigates).

Because the read-only renderer is shared, the markdown live preview and the LLM chat panel get the same gesture.

## Handler (`type_widgets/text/utils.ts`)

`setupContentExpansion(container, { codeBlocks })` is one delegated `dblclick`/`click` listener on the content root, installed next to the image handler in `ReadOnlyText` (`codeBlocks: true`) and `EditableText` (`codeBlocks: false`). A pure `resolveExpansionTarget(target, opts)` maps the event target to either a navigation or a `ContentLightboxData` payload, in a fixed order: anchors, buttons and the Mermaid source textarea are ignored; an included Mermaid note is matched before the code-block shapes so it is never mistaken for one; math resolves only once KaTeX has produced its output.

The read-only content root is a persistent element whose layout effect re-runs on every content change, so the existing image handler accumulated a duplicate listener per re-render (every keystroke in the markdown preview). Both installers now use namespaced events with `.off()` before `.on()`, and a spec pins one navigation after two installs.

Mermaid SVGs are serialised for the lightbox with every occurrence of the diagram id rewritten to `<id>-lightbox`: mermaid scopes its `<style>` rules to `#id` and prefixes marker ids and `url(#…)` refs with it, so the copy never resolves to the original, which can sit inside a collapsed include. A `viewBox` is turned into explicit `width`/`height` and the inline `max-width` dropped, for the `pie` case that mermaid renders with `useMaxWidth: true`.

## Lightbox (`dialogs/content_lightbox.tsx`)

An event-summoned, lazily registered `Modal` (`showContentLightbox` command, size `xl`, full page on mobile). Diagrams and formulas render through `RawHtmlBlock` (not the sanitising variant: the markup already lived in the document and DOMPurify would strip the `<style>` and `foreignObject` mermaid depends on) inside `ZoomPanViewer` in measure mode. The body height is set on `.modal-body` so the viewer's own `height: 100%` chain resolves against a definite size.

## `ZoomPanViewer` (extracted from `ImageViewer`)

The image note's zoom/pan viewport, overlay zoom buttons and keyboard control are now a generic `ZoomPanViewer` with children; `ImageViewer` composes it with identical public props and its spec passes unedited. A new `fit="measure"` mode lays the content out at natural size, measures it against the viewport, and drives the fit through `initialScale`, so `resetTransform()` (the `%` button, the `/` key, double-click) returns to the fitted, centred view. The content stays hidden until a real (non-zero) measurement lands, so asynchronously sized content never paints one frame at scale 1. `computeFitScale` is exported and unit-tested. Verified against the installed react-zoom-pan-pinch 4.2.0.

## Tests

- `type_widgets/text/utils.spec.ts`: 13 new cases (resolver table, ignored targets, `codeBlocks` gate, nested include, idempotent install, click modifiers, print device, SVG serialisation).
- `dialogs/content_lightbox.spec.tsx`: 5 cases (each payload kind, replacement on re-summons, reopen after hide).
- `react/ZoomPanViewer.spec.tsx`: 9 cases (wrapper props, class placement, `ready`, `computeFitScale`, readout, hidden-until-measured, no hint provider without `hints`).
- `ImageViewer.spec.tsx` and `image_viewer_keyboard.spec.ts` unchanged and green. Each new spec was run against a reverted implementation to confirm every assertion fails without it. `pnpm typecheck` clean.

## Not covered here

- **User Guide** (edited via `pnpm edit-docs:edit-docs`, so not in this PR): "Insert buttons" (Mermaid diagram section), "Math Equations", "Developer-specific formatting" / "Code blocks", and "Include Note" should each mention the double-click.
- `fit="measure"` cannot be exercised under happy-dom (zero-sized rects); the fit chain is verified by reading the library, not by a spec. Please try the topology diagram in a real note in both edit and read-only mode, and a formula.
- The CKEditor widget balloon (`z-index` 10000) should hide when focus moves into the modal; if it stays visible over the lightbox in edit mode, the fix is the `zIndex` prop on `Modal`.
- Double-tap on iOS Safari does not synthesise `dblclick`.
- The lightbox body height is desktop-only (`body.desktop`); on mobile the full-page dialog owns the height, which was not checked on a device.

## Deferred polish (from review)

- `evaluateImageZoom(...).pannable` is no longer read in production (the viewer derives it); kept because `ImageViewer.spec.tsx` asserts it.
- `ZOOM_PAN_HINTS` still uses the `image_viewer.hints.*` keys; renaming touches 39 locales.
- Ctrl/middle-click on an included diagram mirrors the image handler, which binds `click`; modern browsers deliver non-primary buttons as `auxclick`, so middle-click is unreachable for both. A follow-up should bind `auxclick` on both installers together.

open_pull_requests.title: feat(scripting): install npm packages for backend scripts
open_pull_requests.body:
Lets scripts use an npm library that the app doesn't ship. A package is resolved to ES modules at install time and stored as a note, so it syncs to every instance, including standalone and mobile. It's loaded the first time a script `require()`s it.

Draft: see **Open items** below.

## Why not `node_modules`

`require()` in backend scripts has been broken in production since the bundler landed. `script_context` kept an allowlist of eight packages and fell back to a dynamic `require`, which resolves against the bundle directory. `dist/node_modules` holds only better-sqlite3 and the tesseract worker chain, so the allowlist worked in a dev checkout and nowhere else. `Server-side imports.md` already conceded the feature was unsupported.

A real installer would mean shipping `pacote` and `@npmcli/arborist` (106 transitive packages, ~1.5 MB minified). It would also serve only two of the four platforms, since standalone and mobile have no filesystem to install into.

## Resolving a package

`script_modules/provider.ts` fetches a package from a build service as browser-ready ES modules. It crawls the module graph and rewrites cross-file specifiers to local names, so the result imports only itself and keeps working long after the service is unreachable. Fetches go through core's request provider, so the server's SSRF hardening and per-response ceiling apply, and the crawl runs unchanged in standalone's worker.

- **Two providers, tried in order:** esm.sh, then jsDelivr. Both serve the same shape (one entry URL plus the graph it links), so a provider is a URL template over one crawler. The fallback is needed in practice: esm.sh cannot build cheerio at `1.0.0` or `1.2.0`. Each provider takes an `origin`, so a self-hosted esm.sh or a jsDelivr mirror is a code-level setting.
- **Strict discovery.** Specifiers are found by pattern, not by parsing, so text that merely reads as a same-origin import is fetched too, and the install fails if it names nothing. A build whose real imports 404 must fail the install rather than land broken.
- **Node.js builds.** `?target=node` on esm.sh leaves built-ins to the host instead of polyfilling them. Both builds of one version can be installed side by side: the portable one serves standalone and mobile, the Node one serves server and desktop.
- **Type declarations.** esm.sh names them in an `x-typescript-types` header, and the same walker crawls them, following `/// <reference>` and resolving a `.js` import to its `.d.ts`. A failed or timed-out declaration costs only that file, and a failed type crawl costs the completions, not the install.

## Storage

Each install is one note under `_scriptModules`, a new hidden-subtree container. The manifest is the note's content and the module sources are attachments under a registered role (`embedded: false`, so content cleanup never erases them).

- **The note id is derived from the package**, so two instances installing the same version before they sync converge on one note.
- **A reinstall writes in place** and drops attachments the rebuild no longer names.
- **A manifest that doesn't parse**, or whose files didn't all survive, reads back as absent.
- **Listing reads only metadata** (size from `LENGTH(blobs.content)`, identity from `blobId`). `openScriptModuleSources()` reads one file when something imports it.

## Installing

A cube button in `NoteActionsCustom` opens **Script modules** on backend, frontend and JSX notes. It sits there rather than in a ribbon tab because that component is mounted by both the new layout and the mobile detail menu. The install route is core-shared, so standalone gets it too. Only the write is wrapped in a transaction, so the fetch never holds one open.

- **Install and remove assert `backendScriptingEnabled`; listing doesn't**, so the dialog can say why the packages are inert.
- **npm search is a row in the field's dropdown** (built on `FormEntryAutocomplete`, #11801), never triggered by typing. A search leaves the instance and tells npmjs.com what someone is looking for, so it runs only when that row is picked. Picking a result fills the field with its exact latest version.

## Loading

- **Backend.** `require()` resolves a child note first, then an installed package, then the host. A package is compiled from ES modules to CommonJS with sucrase (imports only: lowering class fields breaks esm.sh's `buffer` polyfill) and evaluated a file at a time on first use. Cycles resolve the way Node resolves them, and `import.meta` becomes a parameter carrying the file's build URL. Evaluated exports are cached per note against a fingerprint of the files' blob ids.
- **Version selection.** `cheerio` names the single installed version and `cheerio@1.1.2` names that one. A bare name installed at two versions is an error naming both, rather than a guess. Two builds of one version are not an error: the Node build wins wherever Node can run it.
- **Frontend and JSX.** The bundle the page already fetches now carries the packages it requires: only those found by scanning for literal `require` calls, each compiled by the same step. That works on iOS, where nothing can serve a module import of a URL, and keeps sucrase out of the client. A Node-only build resolves to nothing there, and the failure says why.
- **The `require()` gate is a blocklist now, not an allowlist.** The allowlist bought no protection: backend scripts run through `eval()` in-process and reach `globalThis` and `process` directly, which is why `backendScriptingEnabled` is the real boundary. Specifiers normalize to their built-in root, so `node:fs` and `fs/promises` are refused like `fs`. `module`, `inspector` and `repl` join the list, since each reaches the others. A Node build waives the list, which is what it exists for.
- **Errors.** A missing module no longer recites Node's require stack of Trilium's own files.

## Editor

- **Completion of installed package names inside `require("…")`**, and inside `import … from "…"` on JSX notes. A package installed as both builds, or at two versions, appears once, with the versions shown as its detail.
- **Typed `require()`.** Each package is laid out at `/node_modules/<name>/` with a synthesized `package.json`, so TypeScript's CommonJS inference types `require("dayjs")` by itself. A versioned specifier gets a second folder pointing back at the first. Frontend and JSX notes don't see Node-only builds. `skipLibCheck` is on, since a package's declarations belong to a third party.

## LLM skills

The backend and frontend scripting skill sheets now describe the resolution order, installs, version pinning and the blocklist. The model can't install a package, so it's told to write the script as if the package were there and to tell the user the exact spec to install. It's told to prefer a well-known package over hand-rolled logic for parsing, date arithmetic, diffing and templating.

## Docs

`Server-side imports.md` now documents installing from **Script modules**, `require()` by name and by name plus version, and the built-ins that stay refused.

## Tests

Specs cover the provider crawl, storage, the loader, host `require`, frontend collection, the npm registry and the install route under both the server and standalone suites. The dialog, `require()` completion and declaration layout have specs on the client and codemirror sides.

`pnpm typecheck` is clean after the rebase onto `main`. These suites pass:

| Suite | Tests passed |
|---|---|
| Core (server runner) | 134 |
| Core (standalone runner) | 134 |
| Client (feature and related specs) | 133 |
| Codemirror | 393 |

## Open items

- **Docs.** The generated help (`doc_notes`) isn't synced with `Server-side imports.md`. The page doesn't cover frontend and JSX use, Node builds or npm search. It doesn't say that installing contacts esm.sh and jsDelivr and that searching contacts npmjs.com. `Hidden Notes.md` doesn't list `_scriptModules`.
- **Version enforcement.** An unpinned name or a range still installs. It occupies a note keyed on the name alone, so a later reinstall writes a different build into that note and syncs it over the old one. The fix is to split what a person types from what is stored (exact version required), resolving the version through the registry's dist-tags at install time.
- **Cost per `require`.** `requireScriptModule()` lists every install on each `require` a child note doesn't answer, built-ins included.
- **Cost per frontend bundle.** Each frontend bundle fetch recompiles the packages it requires and ships their full source. Caching the compiled output by its fingerprint is the next step.
- **Install path loads at startup.** The server now builds ESM with code splitting, so `provider.ts` and the storage code could move behind a dynamic import.
- **Declaration fetches are sequential, with no overall budget.** Packages with hundreds of declaration files (date-fns, lodash-es) take minutes.
- **Standalone's note cache isn't refreshed on rollback.** This is pre-existing and separate from this PR, but a failed run that touched notes leaves becca dirty there.

The four changes this branch used to carry have landed separately: #11799, #11800, #11801 and #11802.

open_pull_requests.title: fix(llm-chat): treat a done-less SSE body end as an interruption
open_pull_requests.body:
## Summary

**What**

The LLM-chat SSE consumer now tracks whether an explicit `done` or `error` chunk arrived. When the response body ends **without** a terminal chunk, the client reports "LLM stream ended without completing — the connection closed before the response finished (network or proxy interruption)" through the normal error path instead of treating end-of-body as a normal completion.

User aborts still rethrow untouched, and a mid-read failure keeps its specific `LLM stream interrupted: …` message without the missing-terminal message stacking on top of it.

**Why**

#10883 — under poor network conditions (the reporter drives Claude through a TUN-mode proxy), the model's output is sometimes dropped: the chat returns to the "Type a message…" idle state with the prompt intact, no output, and no backend errors logged. A proxy that terminates an SSE connection **cleanly** produces exactly this signature: the browser's `reader.read()` reports `done`, which is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from the server finishing — unless you require the server's own terminal chunk. The server always sends `done` (or a terminal `error`) via `streamToChunks`, so a body end with neither means the response was cut.

**Testing** (`apps/client/src/services/llm_chat.spec.ts`, 25/25):

- New: a body ending after a text chunk with no terminal reports the interruption error (message received but `onDone` never fired) — **verified to fail on the pre-fix consumer** (returns silently).
- New: an `error` chunk as the terminal counts — exactly one `onError`, no stacked missing-terminal message.
- Updated: the optional-callbacks fixture now includes the `done` chunk the server always sends (its omission was an unrealistic fixture shape my change correctly rejects).
- Existing abort/read-failure semantics pinned by the unchanged neighboring tests.

Fixes #10883

open_pull_requests.title: CardDAV address book server as a backend script (prototype)
open_pull_requests.body:
## What this is

A NextCloud-style address book that CardDAV clients (DAVx⁵, iOS/macOS Contacts, Thunderbird) can sync against, implemented **entirely as a Trilium backend script** (`apps/script-deployer/scripts/carddav.ts`, a `#customRequestHandler` note) — deliberately, to probe the limits of the scripting system. The gaps that surfaced are recorded in the developer guide: *Interoperability / "CardDAV prototype and scripting gaps"*.

## Data model — one note per contact

- An address book is any note with `#carddavAddressBook`. On first use the script provisions a "Contacts" `book` collection (table view) with inheritable promoted attribute definitions.
- A contact is a child note: `FN` ↔ note title, `NOTE` ↔ note content, and `EMAIL`/`TEL`/`ORG`/`TITLE`/`BDAY`/`URL`/`ADR`/`CATEGORIES`/`N`/`UID` map to labels — so `#email *=* "@acme.com"` search works and promoted email/phone fields render mailto/tel buttons.
- Unmapped vCard properties round-trip via `#vcardExtra` (except `PHOTO`).

## Protocol subset

`OPTIONS`, `PROPFIND` (depth 0/1), `REPORT` (`addressbook-query`, `addressbook-multiget`), `GET`, `PUT` with `If-Match`/`If-None-Match`, `DELETE`; principal/home-set discovery, per-contact ETags, collection CTag; HTTP Basic auth against a `#carddavPassword` label on the script note. No `sync-collection` REPORT (clients fall back to CTag polling) and no `/.well-known/carddav` (scripts cannot register routes outside `/custom`), so clients need the explicit base URL `http://<host>/custom/carddav/`.

## Enablers fixed along the way

- **`apps/server/src/app.ts`**: `express.text()` now also accepts `text/*`, `application/xml`, `application/*+xml` — bodies of those types never reached (synchronous) custom handlers; `req.body` stayed `undefined`.
- **`packages/trilium-core/src/services/script_context.ts`**: allow `require("zlib")` — the existing sample scripts already import it and failed at runtime under the module allowlist.
- **script-deployer**: deploy `#customRequestHandler` from front matter; enable backend scripting in the dev instance; fix the fresh-database startup path (`cls` was used before `initializeCore()` ran — the server now starts first, like the setup wizard).
- `scripts/probe.ts`: minimal custom-handler echo script used to verify method routing and body parsing.

## Testing

- Verified end-to-end against the script-deployer dev instance with curl driving the request shapes DAVx⁵ uses: discovery chain, address-book auto-provisioning, contact create/read/update/delete (`201`/`204`/`404`/`412`), ETag change on update, stale `If-Match` rejection, multiget with a missing href, unknown-property round-trip, and the Trilium-side note carrying the expected title/labels/promoted definitions.
- `pnpm typecheck` clean; script-deployer (22), custom-route (6), script-context (server + standalone) and all 153 ETAPI specs pass; changed files pass the format config.

## Draft status / open questions

- Real-device DAVx⁵/iOS testing not yet done (curl-level flows only).
- A phone-side edit of a contact's note text replaces rich Trilium content with plain paragraphs (`NOTE` is plain text) — accept, or treat note content as Trilium-only?
- The plaintext `#carddavPassword` label is a stopgap; the gaps report proposes `api.crypto` / ETAPI-token validation for scripts as the proper fix, plus further harness improvements (route-table dispatch for custom handlers, script bundling/testability in script-deployer, opt-in async handlers).

open_pull_requests.title: feat(attributes): select, copy and paste attributes in the sidebar panel
open_pull_requests.body:
Adds selection and a clipboard to the sidebar attributes panel, and reworks how the panel presents its runs of attributes on both a desktop and a phone.

## Selecting and the clipboard

Rows can be picked out — by a checkbox in the kind icon's slot, by a modifier, by a range with shift, by pressing anywhere on a row once picking has started, or by holding a row down on a phone. What can be done to them is said at the foot of the list, in a bar that holds there while the list is scrolled.

Copying writes the attributes as **the text the attributes editor already spells them out in** (`#label=value ~relation=#root/noteId #tag(inheritable)`), so a copy round-trips through that editor, through a note, or out of Trilium entirely. Pasting folds them into the note's own: a name it already carries is replaced, unless its definition says the field holds a set, in which case the pasted value joins what is there.

`getPreprocessedData` moved out of `AttributeEditor` into a new `attribute_clipboard` service, which both surfaces now share.

## The panel's runs

The four cards became one card of folding runs on a desktop — four card headers were a great deal of a hand-wide pane to spend on saying which run is which — gathered by a line drawn down from each heading's chevron, with the count worn as a badge beside the run's name. Collapsed runs are remembered under the keys the cards used, so a pane that had a section put away has it put away still.

A phone keeps the cards it always had. The tree is a pointer's affordance — hairlines, hover, a fold — and the sheet is the width of the screen, so there is no room to save by merging them; each run is a card, with its count in the header and its own way in beside it.

## Mobile fixes found along the way

- The selection bar was drawn **underneath** the rows. Every menu is lifted to `z-index: 3000` on a phone; the rows borrow a menu's dressing, and the rule that un-fixes their position leaves that behind. It does not lie idle as it would on an ordinary static box — the list is a flex item, and a flex item takes its z-index whether positioned or not.
- The bar was also invisible: it composites the card's own wash over the app surface, which lifts it off a right-pane card that paints no ground and hides it against a phone's card that paints precisely that.
- The kind icon's badge was stripped while rows were picked out — a rule clearing the slot for a checkbox a phone never puts there.
- Pasting had no way in at all on a phone, worst of all on a note carrying nothing: no row to hold down means no selection, no bar, and a list with no height to press beside. It is now in the first card's header.

## Testing

- `AttributeList.spec.tsx` — 44 tests
- `AttributeList.mobile.spec.tsx` — 5 tests, new (the device is read once at module load, so the two layouts cannot be told apart in one file)
- `attribute_clipboard.spec.ts` — 17 tests
- Full client suite: 236 files / 2909 tests passing

Behaviour was also checked against a running instance on both a desktop viewport and a phone one; four defects the happy-dom suite could not see were found that way — the stacking above, the surface composition, a CSS cascade specificity bug, and checkbox activation semantics.

open_pull_requests.title: Celandar hideInViews attribute to skip rendering in given views
open_pull_requests.body: This pull request implements a small quality-of-life feature that I've desired in the Trilium calendar, allowing users to hide events in specific view types. Feel free to close this PR if it's deemed unnecessary, but my use case is filtering recurring daily scheduling blocks (e.g. "work" or "sleep") from showing every day in month, year, and list views. I'm using eventDataTransform to set the display of hidden events to "none" based on the view because refetching and filtering in the events getter caused a visible jump after switching views. It seems eventDataTransform is called before rendering, so it's a good time to filter. It's somewhat unfortunate that we must set lazyFetching to false for fullcalendar to call eventDataTransform on view changes, but it also fixes a variety of issues and inconsistencies caused by switching views - like events that span day boundaries being cut off, as seen below after switching to the week view from the month view. It seems to be caused by a problem with fullcalendar that I'll try to make an issue for upstream. I was unsure about the best handling for root calendar views, so date notes currently can't hide themselves - the attribute handling is pretty different in that case, so would it be best to use a generic name like #hideInViews or namespace it like #calendar:hideInViews (which is already used for changing the attribute referenced here)? Additionally, does hiding a parent date note in a view also hide its children? Another question is whether a repeatable attribute like #hideInView is better, but it felt too verbose to me. I'm happy to change it, of course. Thanks again!
